currentContext.expansion: The centrepiece of DOMS' expansion is a 50+ acre greenfield manufacturing complex being developed in phases. The Company has taken possession of the first two buildings, and commercial production is expected to commence towards the end of the second quarter of financial year 2026-27; prolonged and unseasonal monsoon conditions caused a marginal construction delay during the year. Capacity addition at the greenfield complex will commence with wooden pencils, followed by writing instruments, then pencil accessories including erasers and sharpeners, and subsequently scholastic art materials, a phased approach intended to keep capital deployment and asset utilisation efficient while retaining flexibility against changing demand. Management describes the commissioning of this project as a key priority and expects it to enhance operational flexibility, strengthen manufacturing capabilities and support the next phase of growth. Alongside the greenfield build, ongoing brownfield expansion within existing facilities supports near-term capacity requirements: during the year the Company expanded manufacturing capacity for ball point pens, paper stationery, mechanical pencils and adhesives, and made investments across moulding operations, writing instruments, paper stationery and adhesive manufacturing while modernising key manufacturing processes. Capital expenditure during the year was directed towards the phased development of the greenfield facility together with these in-plant capacity additions. The acquisition of Super Treads Private Limited further enhanced paper stationery manufacturing capacity and improved the Company's ability to serve Eastern India. The Company retains a future expansion land bank of 61+ acres and reports a manufacturing footprint of 18 facilities spanning more than 2 million sq. ft. across five locations, with 55+ acres of operations area (as on June 30, 2026). Backward integration continues to deepen, with most key components produced in house so the Company oversees the value chain from design and manufacturing through packaging and distribution. Separately, DOMS has approved a 50:50 joint venture with Seven SpA, part of the F.I.L.A. Group ecosystem, to manufacture premium backpacks, bags and pencil cases, combining Seven's design expertise with DOMS' manufacturing capabilities; it is expected to support export growth and enable premium back-to-school products in the domestic market. BRSR Principle 2 notes capital expenditure incurred towards fire safety systems, sewage treatment plants, water sanitation facilities and electrical infrastructure across facilities.
currentContext.mdna: Domestic business anchors performance, contributing 87.5% of gross product sales, with exports at 12.5% and recording steady double-digit growth|GST rate rationalisation announced in the Union Budget is expected to support consumer demand and accelerate the shift towards the organised sector, a favourable backdrop for trusted branded players|Categories supported by capacity expansions recorded particularly strong momentum, while established categories delivered through product enhancements and improved average selling prices|Healthy demand recorded across Office Supplies, Kits and Combos, Hobby and Craft, Paper Stationery and Back to School, supported by new capacity additions and new product launches|Baby hygiene saw a significant uptick, driven by growing diaper demand and enhanced capacity versus last year|EBITDA margin moderation versus FY2024-25 was primarily attributable to the higher contribution of Uniclan to consolidated operations; PAT margin was impacted by lower finance income from higher utilisation of funds towards capital expenditure|Intercompany exports were impacted during the year by US tariff actions and softer demand in Europe; the easing of tariffs and development of new capacity provide a positive outlook|Input costs linked to crude derivatives have risen since the beginning of the year, met with calibrated pricing and channel margin actions|Operating environment remains influenced by geopolitical developments and volatility in raw material prices|Immediate priority is uninterrupted manufacturing operations and supply chain continuity while carefully managing cost pressures|Indian stationery demand supported by rising literacy, school and college enrolment (NEP 2020, Right to Education), higher disposable income, urbanisation and government education spending|Rapid growth of e-commerce and quick-commerce is expanding stationery accessibility across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities|Premiumisation and personalisation of stationery are lifting demand for branded, customised and design-oriented products|GST exemption on pencils, erasers and exercise books lowers the cost of basic learning materials|Government procurement via GeM and state student-welfare kit schemes (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh) create recurring bulk procurement demand|Intense competition among established brands and emerging players remains a significant challenge for the Indian stationery market|The Indian school bags segment lacks credible widely recognised brands, giving new entrants a large penetration opportunity|Indian diaper market is shifting from episodic use to routine hygiene consumption, aided by rising middle-class incomes, retail expansion and e-commerce reach into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities

risks.risk: Raw material availability and price volatility
risks.note: Non-availability of key raw materials may impact operations, and price fluctuations in polymers, wood, oils, chemicals and pigments may raise production costs and compress margins. Mitigated through long-term supplier relationships, periodic price reviews, strategic inventory buffers, multi-supplier sourcing for critical inputs and backward integration in selected inputs such as wood processing.

risks.risk: Supply chain disruption, trade restrictions and logistics cost inflation
risks.note: Operations depend on timely availability of raw and packaging materials; geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, changes in import/export regulations, global supply chain disruptions and swings in freight and logistics costs can disrupt procurement, raise operating costs and hit export volumes to affected countries. BRSR flags the financial implication as negative. Managed via buffer stock for critical inputs, multi-regional sourcing, extended vendor agreements, a varied base of logistics providers and backup shipping procedures.

risks.risk: Intense competition from domestic and international players
risks.note: Competitive intensity may create pricing pressure and erode market share and profitability. Countered through operational efficiency and cost competitiveness, product innovation, portfolio diversification, strategic partnerships and regular monitoring of market trends.

Variability in product quality, colour consistency or writing performance can damage customer experience, brand reputation and product acceptance - a direct risk for a branded consumer business. Addressed with stringent standards across sourcing, processing, manufacturing, packaging and distribution, dedicated QA/QC teams, defined SOPs and standardised testing, plus reduced dependence on third-party developers.

Operational disruptions or equipment failures may affect production efficiency, product quality and business continuity. Managed through operational controls, preventive maintenance systems and defined safety policies.

risks.risk: Brand protection and intellectual property infringement
risks.note: Infringement of trademarks or designs may dilute brand value and reduce consumer trust, a structural exposure for a company whose moat rests on brand equity. Managed by registering trademarks, designs and copyrights domestically and internationally, monitoring infringements and pursuing legal remedies with channel partners.

risks.risk: People risk - retention of employees and key managerial personnel
risks.note: Employees and KMP are critical to delivering short- and long-term objectives; failure to retain, engage and manage talent could impact business sustainability and operational performance. Managed through training, mentorship, career development, performance feedback, ESOP benefits and diversity, equity and inclusion initiatives.

Operations generate waste, primarily plastic waste, whose disposal is legally regulated; the Company states it is susceptible to fines or legal action in case of violation. Mitigated through a circular manufacturing approach reusing leftover polymers, graphite and calcium carbonate, reuse of packaging, water treatment and recycling, plastic waste handled through authorised recyclers under EPR regulations, hazardous waste through certified agencies and sawdust converted into briquettes.

one-line thesis: DOMS delivered 21.6% FY26 revenue growth driven by new product launches and strong domestic demand, but EBITDA margin compressed to 17.3% due to Uniclan's higher e-commerce costs and 15-20% raw material inflation, with calibrated 4-5% pricing actions taken; the company is investing INR250-275cr in FY27 capex to double manufacturing footprint and maintain market share amid volatility, positioning for sustained growth despite near-term margin pressure.
financial scorecard: revenue: +21.6% YoY (FY26: INR2,326cr); EBITDA/margin: +15.5% YoY (FY26: INR402.6cr, 17.3% vs 18.2% in FY25) — margin drop due to Uniclan’s e-commerce mix and raw material inflation; PAT (rptd): +12.2% YoY (FY26: INR239.6cr); PAT (normalized): Not disclosed — but PAT margin held at 10.3% despite lower other income from capex cash deployment; order book: Not disclosed; net debt: Not disclosed — capex of INR292cr in FY26 implies increased leverage, but no net debt figure provided.
guidance: revenue growth: 17-20% in FY27; margin: No specific guidance — near-term pressure expected due to raw material volatility, but long-term 17-18% EBITDA margin target intact; order inflow: Not specified; capex/commissioning: INR250-275cr in FY27; 45-acre plant Phase 1 to commence commercial production end-Q2 FY27; additional capacity in moulding, writing instruments, and wooden pencils.
segment / subsidiary detail: Core stationery: +19% Q4 growth, driven by back-to-school demand and new SKUs in pencil boxes, school bags, pens, mechanical pencils, stamp pads; office supplies: strong growth in ballpoint pens and highlighters; baby hygiene (Uniclan): Q4 revenue INR55.9cr, EBITDA margin 6.3% (down from 12% in Q3 due to seasonality and e-commerce cost structure); hobby & craft: high growth; exports: steady double-digit growth despite global headwinds.
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into 225K direct stationery stores and Kirana channels via Uniclan; new product innovation in art materials and kits; potential to capture market share from Chinese imports due to rupee depreciation; 45-acre plant (2M sq ft) to double manufacturing capacity by FY29; Uniclan to launch new diaper SKUs for margin expansion.
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin stable at 43.6% FY26; EBITDA margin fell to 17.3% (FY25: 18.2%) due to Uniclan’s higher e-commerce SG&A and 15-20% raw material inflation (40% crude-linked); 4-5% pricing actions taken, but gap remains; baby hygiene segment’s e-commerce mix increased S&D costs, pressuring EBITDA despite stable gross margin.
capex / expansion: FY26: INR292cr (45-acre plant, land acquisitions in Umargam/Jammu, moulding & writing instrument capacity); FY27 guidance: INR250-275cr — focused on moulding, wooden pencils, and phased development of 45-acre facility (commercial production end-Q2 FY27); total capex over next 3 years to fully utilize 45 acres + adjacent land parcels.
capital allocation: Prioritizing capex for capacity expansion (70%+ of outlay) over dividends or buybacks; disciplined approach to pricing to protect market share; cash deployed to capex reduced other income; long-term target: 10% EBITDA margin for Uniclan; no mention of debt reduction or shareholder returns.
risks & watch-items: Geopolitical volatility in West Asia driving crude-linked raw material inflation (15-20%); delayed capex execution or cost overruns; e-commerce cost structure permanently pressuring Uniclan margins; failure to fully pass on inflation without losing share; competition from Chinese imports (though rupee depreciation may help); dependency on seasonal demand (BTS, baby hygiene).
management quality / tone: Confident and disciplined — emphasized long-term brand equity, calibrated pricing, market share protection over short-term margin recovery; acknowledged near-term margin pressure but framed it as temporary; reiterated commitment to capex and capacity building; tone was cautious on guidance but optimistic on structural growth drivers.
non-obvious takeaways: Despite 15-20% raw material inflation, gross margin held steady due to strategic inventory stocking — implying strong supply chain foresight; Uniclan’s 8.6% FY26 EBITDA margin is already 115% above acquisition target (4-5%), suggesting superior integration; 4M YouTube subs and 170K Instagram followers indicate a rare consumer-brand bond in stationery, enabling pricing power; the INR30 pack-of-5 pen pricing strategy cleverly masks MRP hikes from coinage issues — a behavioral pricing innovation.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: DOMS Industries is a kid-centric consumer company and one of India's leading branded stationery and art material manufacturers, extending from scholastic stationery into art materials, back-to-school products and baby hygiene.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: DOMS manufactures, markets and distributes stationery and art material products, with a portfolio spanning scholastic stationery, scholastic art materials, paper stationery, office supplies, hobby and craft, fine art materials, back-to-school products, kits and combos and baby hygiene. It sells across nine product categories and over 4,800 SKUs to kids, students, young adults, office professionals, artists and creative enthusiasts. Products reach consumers in India through super stockists, distributors, retailers, modern trade, e-commerce and quick-commerce, and internationally through merchants, trading houses and the FILA Group network.

guidance.title: Guidance
guidance.body: revenue growth: 17-20% in FY27; margin: No specific guidance — near-term pressure expected due to raw material volatility, but long-term 17-18% EBITDA margin target intact; order inflow: Not specified; capex/commissioning: INR250-275cr in FY27; 45-acre plant Phase 1 to commence commercial production end-Q2 FY27; additional capacity in moulding, writing instruments, and wooden pencils.

growth_optionality.title: Growth verticals / optionality
growth_optionality.body: Expansion into 225K direct stationery stores and Kirana channels via Uniclan; new product innovation in art materials and kits; potential to capture market share from Chinese imports due to rupee depreciation; 45-acre plant (2M sq ft) to double manufacturing capacity by FY29; Uniclan to launch new diaper SKUs for margin expansion.

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Domestic business anchors performance, contributing 87.5% of gross product sales, with exports at 12.5% and recording steady double-digit growth
- GST rate rationalisation announced in the Union Budget is expected to support consumer demand and accelerate the shift towards the organised sector, a favourable backdrop for trusted branded players
- Categories supported by capacity expansions recorded particularly strong momentum, while established categories delivered through product enhancements and improved average selling prices
- Healthy demand recorded across Office Supplies, Kits and Combos, Hobby and Craft, Paper Stationery and Back to School, supported by new capacity additions and new product launches
- Baby hygiene saw a significant uptick, driven by growing diaper demand and enhanced capacity versus last year
- EBITDA margin moderation versus FY2024-25 was primarily attributable to the higher contribution of Uniclan to consolidated operations; PAT margin was impacted by lower finance income from higher utilisation of funds towards capital expenditure
- Intercompany exports were impacted during the year by US tariff actions and softer demand in Europe; the easing of tariffs and development of new capacity provide a positive outlook
- Input costs linked to crude derivatives have risen since the beginning of the year, met with calibrated pricing and channel margin actions
- Operating environment remains influenced by geopolitical developments and volatility in raw material prices
- Immediate priority is uninterrupted manufacturing operations and supply chain continuity while carefully managing cost pressures
- Indian stationery demand supported by rising literacy, school and college enrolment (NEP 2020, Right to Education), higher disposable income, urbanisation and government education spending
- Rapid growth of e-commerce and quick-commerce is expanding stationery accessibility across Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities
- Premiumisation and personalisation of stationery are lifting demand for branded, customised and design-oriented products
- GST exemption on pencils, erasers and exercise books lowers the cost of basic learning materials
- Government procurement via GeM and state student-welfare kit schemes (Telangana, Andhra Pradesh) create recurring bulk procurement demand
- Intense competition among established brands and emerging players remains a significant challenge for the Indian stationery market
- The Indian school bags segment lacks credible widely recognised brands, giving new entrants a large penetration opportunity
- Indian diaper market is shifting from episodic use to routine hygiene consumption, aided by rising middle-class incomes, retail expansion and e-commerce reach into Tier-2 and Tier-3 cities

margins.title: Margins & cost dynamics
margins.body: Gross margin stable at 43.6% FY26; EBITDA margin fell to 17.3% (FY25: 18.2%) due to Uniclan’s higher e-commerce SG&A and 15-20% raw material inflation (40% crude-linked); 4-5% pricing actions taken, but gap remains; baby hygiene segment’s e-commerce mix increased S&D costs, pressuring EBITDA despite stable gross margin.

capital_allocation.title: Capital allocation
capital_allocation.body: Prioritizing capex for capacity expansion (70%+ of outlay) over dividends or buybacks; disciplined approach to pricing to protect market share; cash deployed to capex reduced other income; long-term target: 10% EBITDA margin for Uniclan; no mention of debt reduction or shareholder returns.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: The centrepiece of DOMS' expansion is a 50+ acre greenfield manufacturing complex being developed in phases. The Company has taken possession of the first two buildings, and commercial production is expected to commence towards the end of the second quarter of financial year 2026-27; prolonged and unseasonal monsoon conditions caused a marginal construction delay during the year. Capacity addition at the greenfield complex will commence with wooden pencils, followed by writing instruments, then pencil accessories including erasers and sharpeners, and subsequently scholastic art materials, a phased approach intended to keep capital deployment and asset utilisation efficient while retaining flexibility against changing demand. Management describes the commissioning of this project as a key priority and expects it to enhance operational flexibility, strengthen manufacturing capabilities and support the next phase of growth. Alongside the greenfield build, ongoing brownfield expansion within existing facilities supports near-term capacity requirements: during the year the Company expanded manufacturing capacity for ball point pens, paper stationery, mechanical pencils and adhesives, and made investments across moulding operations, writing instruments, paper stationery and adhesive manufacturing while modernising key manufacturing processes. Capital expenditure during the year was directed towards the phased development of the greenfield facility together with these in-plant capacity additions. The acquisition of Super Treads Private Limited further enhanced paper stationery manufacturing capacity and improved the Company's ability to serve Eastern India. The Company retains a future expansion land bank of 61+ acres and reports a manufacturing footprint of 18 facilities spanning more than 2 million sq. ft. across five locations, with 55+ acres of operations area (as on June 30, 2026). Backward integration continues to deepen, with most key components produced in house so the Company oversees the value chain from design and manufacturing through packaging and distribution. Separately, DOMS has approved a 50:50 joint venture with Seven SpA, part of the F.I.L.A. Group ecosystem, to manufacture premium backpacks, bags and pencil cases, combining Seven's design expertise with DOMS' manufacturing capabilities; it is expected to support export growth and enable premium back-to-school products in the domestic market. BRSR Principle 2 notes capital expenditure incurred towards fire safety systems, sewage treatment plants, water sanitation facilities and electrical infrastructure across facilities.

management_tone.body: Confident and disciplined — emphasized long-term brand equity, calibrated pricing, market share protection over short-term margin recovery; acknowledged near-term margin pressure but framed it as temporary; reiterated commitment to capex and capacity building; tone was cautious on guidance but optimistic on structural growth drivers.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Diversified portfolio across nine product categories and over 4,800 SKUs, reducing dependence on any single category
- Established brand portfolio - DOMS, C3, Amariz, Fixy Fix, Clapjoy, Wowper and Reynolds - with strong brand recall and consumer trust built over two decades
- Modern, scalable and backward-integrated manufacturing network of 18 facilities across five locations spanning more than 2 million sq. ft., supporting quality, cost efficiency and supply-chain resilience
- Extensive multi-channel distribution: more than 130 super stockists, over 6,250 distributors, over 1,45,000 retail outlets and a sales force of over 1,000, plus Uniclan's separate network of 95+ super stockists, 1,300+ distributors and 55,000+ retail outlets
- In-house R&D and product engineering at Umbergaon with a research and design team of over 60 professionals and a quality assurance team of more than 175
- Strategic partnership with F.I.L.A. - Fabbrica Italiana Lapis ed Affini S.p.A. giving access to a global distribution network and exclusive marketing rights for F.I.L.A. Group products across seven countries
- Recognised by the Pen & Stationery Association of India as the No. 1 Exporter for the fourth consecutive year, with exports to 55+ countries
- Track record of bolt-on acquisitions extending the platform into paper stationery, packaging, toys, school bags and baby hygiene

other.title: Notable from the deck
other.body:
- [Acquisition - Reynolds] Acquired the 'Reynolds' brand and related assets in 2026: worldwide registered trademarks and domain names, patents and designs (proprietary moulds and product designs), machinery and equipment (excluding land and building), inventory, novation of key customer and supplier contracts, and the Reynolds sales and marketing teams. Asset Purchase Agreement implementation is underway with team integration completed; full sales potential is expected to be realised over time as integration progresses and Reynolds manufacturing commences.
- [M&A track record] Serial acquirer: R.R. Industries and S. Tech Industries (2011), 51% of Pioneer Stationery (2015-16, paper stationery), 30.0% of Clapjoy Innovations (2023, toys), 75.0% of Micro Wood (2023, tin and paper packaging), 51.0% of Skido Industries (2024, bags), 51.8% of Uniclan Healthcare (2024, baby hygiene), 51.0% of Super Treads (2025, paper stationery).
- [F.I.L.A. partnership] Exclusive rights to export DOMS products in F.I.L.A.'s existing areas of presence, exclusive marketing rights in 7 countries for F.I.L.A. Group products, OEM manufacturing for the F.I.L.A. Group, and access to its product formulations and global trend knowledge; F.I.L.A. is described with 100+ years' industry experience, presence in 150+ countries, 25 brands and revenues of 572 Euro Mn (as of FY25 ending Dec 31, 2025).
- [Input cost headwind] The deck attributes margin moderation in the quarter to a significant increase and volatility in raw material costs driven by the Middle East conflict and broader global uncertainties, alongside a new tranche of ESOP grants and headcount added for the upcoming new facility.
- [Governance] Chairman Massimo Candela and non-executive directors Annalisa Barbera and Luca Pelosin sit alongside promoter-group whole-time directors and MD Santosh Raveshia, reflecting the F.I.L.A. relationship at board level.
